record.original_question: Besides the currently known examples, are there other arrangements of distinct complex projective lines with the property that no point is incident to exactly two of the lines?

evidence.quote: Question 3.4. Are there other complex line arrangements having no points where exactly two lines meet?

artifact.status_search_result: The classification of complex line arrangements with no double points (t_2 = 0) is a well-known open problem. By Sylvester–Gallai, no nontrivial real example exists, but a few families of complex examples (pencils, dual Hesse, Fermat/Ceva arrangements) are known, and no proof that these are the only ones has been established. The problem is recorded as open in survey notes and talks on line arrangements.

status_evidence.title: Some open questions about line arrangements in the projective plane
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem to classify all complex line arrangements with t_2 = 0; only a few known families exist.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of complex line arrangements with no double points is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The role of line arrangements in some open problems in algebraic geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Three nontrivial kinds of complex line arrangements are known with t_2 = 0, but there is no proof these are the only ones.
status_evidence.claim: Only a handful of complex arrangements with t_2 = 0 are known, and whether others exist remains open.
